students.name: Amina Rahman
students.capability: Fast pace. Facts through 12 are automatic. A spoken list of steps fades within a minute.
students.reached: She took the picture and finished while the spoken directions were still going.
students.fellApart: With the picture removed and only the voice left, she lost the second step.
memory: Week 1: she finished from the picture and lost the second step when only the voice was left.
Last week she drew a correct area model for multi-digit multiplication and skipped the written partial products. Listening without a picture, she missed a step.

students.name: Theo Lang
students.capability: Steady pace. Holds a chant. Drops facts and steps when the work goes silent.
students.reached: He chose the spoken version and could repeat it after one hearing.
students.fellApart: The same task on a silent page, and the procedure dropped out halfway.
memory: Week 1: he repeated the spoken version after one hearing and lost it on a silent page.
The harder multiplication facts stuck as a skip-count chant. On a timed silent sheet those facts were gone.

students.name: Lila Nguyen
students.capability: Deliberate pace. Facts are solid through the 5s. The idea slips if the objects are cleared too soon.
students.reached: She went straight for the blocks and built the answer correctly.
students.fellApart: When the blocks were put away before she wrote, the written answer no longer matched what she had built.
memory: Week 1: the blocks were right, and the written answer was wrong after the blocks were cleared.
She showed 12 × 4 with bags of cubes. The product on the paper was wrong after the cubes were cleared first.

students.name: Jonah Ellis
students.capability: Steady pace. Writes well above grade. Place value slips when a sentence forgets the units. Being wrong in front of the class throws him.
students.reached: He chose the page and wrote a clear account.
students.fellApart: The account sounded right and still used the wrong unit, and he would not say so in front of the group.
memory: Week 1: the writing was clear and the unit was still wrong. He would not correct it out loud.
He wrote a clean explanation of rounding and then rounded 1,450 to 1,000. The sentences never said whether the digits were thousands or hundreds.

students.name: Mateo Cruz
students.capability: Deliberate pace. Strong estimate. Working memory holds about two steps, then the rest falls off.
students.reached: He started willingly and got the first two moves right when they were shown one at a time.
students.fellApart: Given the whole procedure at once, the third step vanished even though the first two had been correct.
memory: Week 1: two moves shown one at a time held. The whole procedure at once lost step three.
Two-step word problems hold. Three-step problems fail on the third step. He gets that step back when it arrives alone, after the first two are done.
